extracted.intended_audience: TikTok creators, social media marketers, and video-first content producers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and evaluation criteria for creating TikTok videos optimized for the platform's 2026 recommendation priorities (watch time, authenticity, niche authority), including posting tactics, creative patterns, and use of AI tools for clipping and optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core recommendation goal: maximize watch time and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok's algorithm is designed around a single goal: maximize watch time and engagement by showing the right content to the right person at the right time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize producing content that keeps viewers watching longer rather than chasing raw view counts. Examples: a video with 10,000 views and 80% average completion will outperform a video with 100,000 views and 20% completion in long-term distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-Stage Testing Process
rubrics_metrics.description: When you post a video, the algorithm follows a systematic testing process: Stage 1 (Initial Test Pool, First 1-3 hours), Stage 2 (Performance Evaluation, First 6-24 hours), Stage 3 (Progressive Scaling, 24-72 hours), Stage 4 (For You Page Placement, Ongoing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand each stage to optimize early signals (first-hour engagement) and sustain momentum across waves of distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three Primary Ranking Factors (weights)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three categories of signals determine content performance: 1) User Interactions (Highest Weight: ~70%), 2) Video Information (Medium Weight: ~20%), 3) Device and Account Settings (Lower Weight: ~10%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate effort primarily to improving user interaction signals (completion, re-watches, shares) while optimizing video metadata and respecting device/account context.

rubrics_metrics.name: User Interactions (highest weight ~70%)
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithm tracks every action users take with your content. Strongest signals include watch time and completion rate, re-watches and loops, shares (weighted 3x higher than likes), and saves. Medium signals: comments (especially long threads), likes, follows, profile visits. Negative signals: 'Not Interested', reports, immediate scrolls, and high drop-off rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design content to maximize completion, encourage re-watches and shares, and prompt saves. Avoid tactics that create immediate scroll behavior. Treat shares and saves as high-value outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Information (medium weight ~20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithm analyzes captions and on-screen text, sounds/music, hashtags (declined importance), visual elements/filters, video length and pacing. It assigns topic clusters and interest categories for recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your topic clear via captions/on-screen text and consistent visual markers so the algorithm can categorize your content and confidently recommend it to interested audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device and Account Settings (lower weight ~10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Background contextual signals include language preference, country setting, device type (Android vs iOS), account age and activity patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that localization and account maturity affect distribution; new accounts receive different treatment in their first 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch Time Dominates Everything (2025 shift)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2025 data shows watch time has become the dominant signal: creators who maintain viewer attention see substantially higher growth and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus creative energy on producing fewer, higher-quality videos that maximize retention rather than high-frequency low-value posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-Hour Engagement Criticality
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithm gives significantly more weight to interactions within the first 60 minutes after posting; strong first-hour engagement leads to aggressive early scaling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize posting time, have engaged community members ready, respond quickly to comments, and use cross-platform traffic in the first hour to boost signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche Consistency / 90-Day Commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The algorithm increasingly rewards creators who consistently serve a specific community. Recommendation: choose a specific content category and commit exclusively for at least 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid posting across 3+ unrelated topics. Use niche-specific language, visual identity, and content markers to build algorithmic confidence and compound authority over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longer Videos Gain Traction (shift toward 60-180 seconds)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok is testing longer formats; videos in the 60-180 second range may receive preferential distribution over very short clips, provided retention is maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for engaging-form content where length is justified by retention; create clear hook-to-payoff structures and consider multi-part series for episodic momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic human content over overly polished production
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic, behind-the-scenes, talking-head, and 'raw' content styles see higher engagement than heavy production; authenticity signals trustworthiness to the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show real faces, real voice, and process. Use editing to enhance clarity and pacing but avoid producing content that feels inauthentic for the niche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Moderation & Advertiser-Friendly Prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: Under new US ownership, expect stricter moderation and an algorithmic prioritization of safe, brand-friendly content attractive to advertisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor educational, inspirational, and family-friendly content; be transparent about sponsored content and consider toning down controversial hooks if relying on algorithmic distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-commerce & Shoppable Content Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok is increasingly integrating commerce; live shopping, product demonstrations, affiliate content, and 'Shop Now' CTA content may receive algorithmic boosts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even non-sellers should consider product education, honest reviews, and natural commerce integrations that drive measurable purchasing behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity Verification & Combatting AI-Generated Content
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok may implement measures to identify and deprioritize fully AI-generated videos while boosting verifiably human-created content; expected signals include face/voice verification, creation-proof, labeling requirements, and expanded account verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show your face and voice consistently, occasionally document creation processes, and disclose AI-assistance when required. Use AI tools to enhance human content rather than fully replace humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Algorithm Variations (localization matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: With Oracle managing the US algorithm separately, regional differences in content priorities, moderation, and feature sets are likely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target and optimize for your primary geographic market (language, references, trends) rather than assuming global parity; adapt content for region-specific audiences if cross-posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize for Watch Time: Hook strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective hook patterns to maximize initial retention: Question Hook, Contradiction Hook, Results Hook, Story Hook—each designed to create curiosity or promise value and keep viewers watching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a compelling promise or question in the first 0-10 seconds. Match hook type to content format (educational, opinion, case study, entertainment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining Watch Time: Pattern Interrupt & Progressive Value
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain engagement by changing visual/audio elements every 10-15 seconds (pattern interrupt) and delivering incremental value across the video (hook → insights → payoff).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure seconds 0-10 hook, 10-30 first insight, 30-50 stronger insight, final payoff; use cuts, zooms, text overlays, and audio shifts to re-capture attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Endings That Encourage Re-watches
rubrics_metrics.description: End with cliffhangers, callbacks, pattern breaks, or clear CTAs to encourage re-watches and further engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cliffhangers for series, tie endings back to hooks with a twist, and include follow/CTA prompts that incentivize interaction and re-viewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools for identifying high-retention moments (e.g., OpusClip)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than guessing, use analytics or AI tools to extract proven high-retention segments from long-form videos for repurposing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload long-form source content to analytics/AI tools that detect hooks, punchlines, and fully-contained moments to create clips with pre-validated retention characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting Time Strategy Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Three methods: Peak Audience Time (post when followers active), Off-Peak Testing (low-competition hours like 2-4 AM EST), and Rapid Testing (systematically test multiple times over 30 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analytics to find your 3-hour window, test off-peak windows for reduced competition, and track first-hour engagement vs final reach to identify optimal times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Acceleration Tactics for the first hour
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-posting prep (schedule, have engaged members ready), first 15-min actions (reply to every comment, pin engaging comment), first-hour scaling (share cross-platform, engage with other creators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan precise community-engagement steps for the immediate post period to maximize early signals: prompt replies, seed conversation, and cross-post strategically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche-Specific Content Markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Signals that convey niche authority: industry terminology, assumed context (don't over-explain basics), consistent filming setup, brand templates, and aesthetic choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use jargon and a consistent visual identity to signal category expertise to both audiences and the algorithm; assume some audience knowledge to attract more advanced viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche Community Engagement & Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Daily meaningful engagement with other creators in your exact niche (commenting, duets, collaborations) builds relationships and algorithmic momentum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spend time each day leaving substantive comments, create duets/replies, and organize collaborative series to drive cross-traffic and reciprocal engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Web Strategy (interconnected content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create content that references and links to other videos ('last week I covered X...'), driving profile visits, binge-watching, and follow conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure serial content and recurring themes that encourage viewers to watch multiple videos on your profile, increasing total watch time and follow likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Trending Sounds Authentically (trend participation hierarchy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all trend participation is equal: Tier 1 Early Authentic Adoption (best), Tier 2 Authentic Late Adoption (medium), Tier 3 Forced Trend-Jacking (low).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only adopt trending sounds if you can adapt them authentically to your niche and add unique value. Use Creative Center and niche creators to spot early trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original Sounds as Brand Building
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating signature sounds or catchphrases builds audio branding; when others use your sound it signals authority to the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop memorable audio elements that align with your niche and encourage reuse by other creators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments are more valuable than likes
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments indicate stronger interest, increase time spent, and generate conversations; videos with high comment ratios outperform those with many likes but few comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design content that invites comments (question-style prompts, polarizing but authentic opinions, fill-in-the-blank hooks). Respond substantively to comments and pin high-value threads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment Response Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first hour respond to every comment with substantial replies (15-30 words), ask follow-ups, pin engaging comments, and create reply videos to popular threads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize generating conversational threads and use video replies to amplify popular comments and drive additional watch time.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 5-to-1 Community Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For every video you post, commit to leaving 5 meaningful comments on other creators' videos in your niche to build visibility and reciprocity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice increases profile exposure and fosters relationships that can lead to collaborations and cross-promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop Doing: Hashtag Stuffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using 20-30 generic hashtags (#fyp #viral). The algorithm shifted away from hashtag-heavy ranking toward caption content and visual analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 3-5 targeted, specific hashtags and write descriptive captions in natural language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop Doing: Trend-Hopping Without Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't participate in every trend regardless of fit; forced adoption can harm niche authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 1-2 trends per month that authentically fit and add unique value; skip trends that dilute your category signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop Doing: Sub-10-Second Videos (when aiming for watch-time optimization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ultra-short clips underperform when the algorithm prioritizes absolute watch time over simple completion rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce 30-90 second videos with sustained retention to generate more total watch time per viewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop Doing: Buying Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchased followers/likes/comments are detectable and often penalized by the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build genuine engagement through consistent, valuable content and authentic community interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop Doing: Posting and Ghosting
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting content without responding to comments or engaging with others reduces creator engagement signals and distribution potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate time after posting to engage and maintain a daily engagement routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop Doing: Copying Viral Videos Exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplicate, shot-for-shot reproductions of viral videos are identified and deprioritized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study viral formats and adapt them with unique perspective and niche-specific twists rather than exact copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpusClip strategy: create long-form source + extract clips
rubrics_metrics.description: Workflow: produce substantial 10-30 minute source videos, upload to OpusClip to identify high-engagement segments, extract and optimize 10-20 clips, and distribute 3-5 times weekly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach scales volume without burnout, preserves authenticity, maintains niche consistency, and targets algorithmic quality signals like retention and complete thoughts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated optimization practices (captions, reframing, titles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tools that add animated captions for accessibility/engagement, reframe to TikTok dimensions, and suggest clip titles based on content analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply brand templates and automated captioning to increase accessibility and initial watchability while reviewing outputs for voice/accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced tooling features to scale production
rubrics_metrics.description: Features like ClipAnything (natural language search of moments), AI B-roll integration, brand templates, and team collaboration help scale content production and maintain consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt tools that support fast extraction, consistent branding, and collaborative workflows when managing multiple creators or clients.
